subject: Supply-chain flowdown: vendor subcontracting approval & DPA questions
messages:
From: Contracts Team <contracts@edgebridge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Supply chain notice: proposed subcontracting of DeepCloud (subprocessor)

Hi Kimberly,

Following our onboarding checklist: EdgeBridge intends to engage DeepCloud LLC as a subprocessor for telemetry aggregation on the agent component that will touch customer PII. Per our MSA, we are providing the flow-down notice and the DPA addendum for your review.

Attached: edgebridge_flowdown_notice.pdf (PDF) — includes the proposed subprocessor DPA and the requested DPA signature block.

Key items:
- Data residency: logs will be processed in us-west region, backups in eu-west.
- Audit rights: DeepCloud requests SOC report access to third parties, proposes quarterly sampling rather than full audit.
- Liability: EdgeBridge proposes liability cap equal to Order Form value; DeepCloud asks for carveout limiting liability for subcontractor work.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the proposed flow-down terms or if you require redlines/consent form changes. Our timeline: we are aiming for an executed flowdown by EOD Friday 2026-11-05 to meet our implementation window.

Thanks,
Alejandra Ruiz
Senior Contracts Manager | EdgeBridge
alejandra.ruiz@edgebridge.com

--
Attachment: edgebridge_flowdown_notice.pdf (1 page)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference>

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supply chain notice: proposed subcontracting of DeepCloud (subprocessor)

Thanks Alejandra — appreciate the heads-up. Looping in our legal and procurement leads for quick review: Rishi (legal) and Marissa (procurement). Dev — fyi for any infra constraints on data residency.

High-level asks from our side:
- Rishi: can you flag any absolute dealbreakers in their proposed DPA? In particular, audit scope and liability carveouts.
- Marissa: what is our procurement approval path and expected lead time for a consent to subcontract?
- Dev: confirm we can accept the proposed region split (us-west processing / eu-west backups) without additional controls.

Alejandra — we will aim to revert with a consolidated reply + any redline within 48 hrs. If we need to negotiate, we will call you to keep on the Friday deadline.

Best,
Kimberly
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@edgebridge.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Supply chain notice: proposed subcontracting of DeepCloud (subprocessor)

Kimberly / team — reviewed the flowdown and DPA. Quick summary and recommended redlines:

1) Audit rights: EdgeBridge/DeepCloud's quarterly sampling proposal is insufficient for our Tier-1 customers. We should push for: (a) right to conduct audits annually (or upon reasonable suspicion), and (b) right to review SOC2 or equivalent reports with appropriate NDA.

2) Data residency & cross-border transfers: If backups land in eu-west, we need explicit guarantees of encryption at rest + contractual cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs or equivalent). Add a clause confirming encryption keys are controlled by EdgeBridge and not accessible to DeepCloud without mutual consent.

3) Liability carveouts for subcontractors: We cannot accept a carveout that reduces EdgeBridge's liability to our customers. Request a flow-down that keeps EdgeBridge fully liable for subcontractor acts (typical flowdown language: vendor remains responsible for subprocessor compliance).

4) Subprocessor list and changes: Add a clause requiring advance notice + 30-day objection right for material new subprocessors.

5) Encryption/crypto: require TLS 1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest, plus key rotation schedule described.

Next steps: I attached a short redline_snippet_MSA.docx (snippet) with suggested language for sections 4 (audit), 6 (subcontracting), and 9 (data transfers). Marissa — if procurement can greenlight the standard consent template, we can push this back to EdgeBridge with our redlines and a consent template for execution.

If EdgeBridge cannot accept these changes, escalate to sales leadership for risk acceptance.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.inference

--
Attachment: redline_snippet_MSA.docx (3 suggested clauses)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>, Contracts Team <contracts@edgebridge.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Supply chain notice: proposed subcontracting of DeepCloud (subprocessor)

Quick procurement note — path to approval and time estimates:

- Standard vendor/subprocessor consent (non-material changes): 2–3 business days once legal provides redline and consent template.
- Material redlines (audit + liability tweaks): requires procurement review + risk signoff; estimate 4–7 business days.

For this flowdown, because Rishi is requesting audit expansion and liability clarification, I classify as "material". That said, we can fast-track if EdgeBridge accepts our suggested narrow language: we will send the consent and request their acceptance of the redline snippet by EOD Thu 2026-11-05.

Action items:
- Rishi: please finalize the short snippet and confirm the specific phrasing for the objection window (I suggest 30 days).
- Kimberly: once Rishi confirms, send to EdgeBridge with the procurement_consent_template.pdf attached. Include a DocuSign link for quick signature.

I'll coordinate billing/PO/Order Form impact once consent is signed.

Marissa Cole
Head of Procurement | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
